title: Asian Games: Treesa-Gayatri enter women’s doubles quarterfinals
indian_angle: Indian women's doubles pair Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand advanced to the quarterfinals of the Asian Games, defeating a strong Japanese pair.
summary: Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand secured a spot in the Asian Games women’s doubles quarterfinals by defeating the World No. 3 Japanese pair. This follows their earlier quarterfinal finish in the women's team event.

title: Sindhu, Ayush, Unnati advance at Asian Games; Lakshya bows out
indian_angle: P.V. Sindhu, Ayush, and Unnati secured wins at the Asian Games, while Lakshya Sen faced an early exit, providing a mixed bag of results for India.
summary: World No. 11 P.V. Sindhu defeated Chinese Taipei’s Chiu Pin-chian 21-19 21-14 to advance in women's singles at the Asian Games. Ayush and Unnati also progressed, but Lakshya Sen was eliminated in the second round.

title: Saina Nehwal: Celebrate non-cricket sports winners equally
indian_angle: Indian badminton icon Saina Nehwal voiced her desire for non-cricket sports winners to receive equal celebration and attention in India.
summary: Olympic and World championships medallist Saina Nehwal discussed the challenges non-cricket sports face for recognition in India, advocating for equal celebration of all athletes. She also touched upon the impending change to badminton’s scoring system and the future of Indian badminton.

title: Satwik-Chirag knocked out in first round of men's doubles
indian_angle: India's top men's doubles pair, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, suffered an unexpected first-round exit, a significant setback for Indian badminton.
summary: The world No. 5 Indian men's doubles pair, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, were defeated in the first round by Thailand's Pakkapon Teeraratsakul and Peeratchai Sukphun.

title: National Camp for BWF World Junior Championships 2026
indian_angle: A national coaching camp is underway in Guwahati to prepare Indian junior players for the upcoming BWF World Junior Championships 2026, highlighting India's investment in future talent.
summary: The Badminton Association of India has organized a national coaching camp at the National Center of Excellence (NCE) in Guwahati for players preparing for the BWF World Junior Championships 2026.
